correctness.rationale: Odd squarefree four-prime n has σ(n)/n<2; hence n=2pqr. Monotone abundancy bounds reduce to p∈{3,5,7} and exactly 12 possible (p,q) pairs, including the nontrivial q≤23 bound when p=3: for q≥29 no omitted divisor contains qr and every three other divisors sum ≤11(1+q+r)<σ(n)−2n=12(1+q+r). For a fixed (p,q), all 15 proper divisors split as 8 d and 7 dr, so every three-term candidate is one of 455 templates with sum Cr+E. The identity σ(2pqr)−2(2pqr)=Ar+B yields (A−C)r=E−B; E<B eliminates an infinitely-degenerate denominator and yields at most one integer r per template. Exact integer arithmetic over 12×455=5,460 templates independently returned 51 integers and 60 distinct unordered witness triples, largest n=12714, and checked proper divisibility/primality and defining identities. The template reduction—not a bounded n scan—is a proof of infinite-family completeness.
residual_risks: Definition means existence of three distinct omitted divisors; does not exclude simultaneous shorter representations.
The result is for exactly four distinct primes and squarefree n; higher support is not constrained.
